question: Shared once the record's misreading is set aside: LMCI vs NC classification from MRI in ADNI. P-71 uses rs-fMRI connectivity at baseline and year 1 (ADNI-2 and ADNI-3). P-79 uses a single time point of rs-fMRI plus T1 grey-matter volumes plus an age/sex population graph (ADNI2). Structural and functional MRI count as one channel, and the two-time-point input, the added T1 features, the architecture and the validation design (LOOCV against stratified 5-fold CV) are differences the rule allows.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy, on the figures the papers print. The record's claim_b ('+8.5% vs baseline') is P-79's average improvement over its own baselines, not an accuracy (condition 6). P-79's task-matched figure is NC vs LMCI 97.44% (AUC 99.75%).

figures.P-71: LOOCV, SGN + SSBi-LSTM. The record's figure is ADNI-2&3 pooled (40 LMCI + 49 NC = 89): fusion of two time points 91.42%, Wilson n = 89 gives [0.838, 0.957]; baseline only 87.14% [0.786, 0.926]; year 1 only 89.28%. ADNI-2 alone (30 LMCI + 33 NC = 63): fusion 92.06% [0.827, 0.966]; baseline only 87.30% [0.769, 0.934].
figures.P-79: Stratified 5-fold CV, ADNI2 (161 NC + 128 LMCI = 289). The record's task-matched headline is Scheme 3 (fMRI + T1 + phenotype) 97.44 +/- 1.85%, Wilson n = 289 gives [0.949, 0.987]. Scheme 2 (fMRI + phenotype, single time point) is 87.59 +/- 5.36%, Wilson [0.833, 0.909]. Scheme 1 (T1 + phenotype) is 84.65%.

matched_figure_check: Both papers report the shared condition, one time point of rs-fMRI. P-71's baseline-only accuracies are 87.30% on ADNI-2 (the cohort P-79 uses) and 87.14% on ADNI-2&3. P-79's fMRI + phenotype scheme gives 87.59%. Each estimate lies inside the others' intervals: 0.8759 is inside [0.769, 0.934] and [0.786, 0.926], and 0.873 is inside [0.833, 0.909]. The matched figures dissolve the gap. The headline gap (91.42% against 97.44%, beyond uncertainty in both directions) comes from the inputs each paper adds. P-79's own ablation attributes about 9.9 points to adding T1 volumes to fMRI, and P-71's own tables attribute about 4-5 points to adding the year-1 scan. The small difference left (P-79's population graph uses age and sex, which P-71's baseline model does not) does not open a gap.
performance_validity: P-79 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion for its headline figure, checked against the source. NC vs LMCI accuracy 97.44% (AUC 99.75%) comes from internal stratified 5-fold CV on 289 subjects (a small-to-modest sample). There is no external MCI cohort: its only external test is a depression dataset (REST-META-MDD, MDD vs healthy controls). P-71 (91.42%, AUC 96.43%, LOOCV on 89 subjects) is below 0.97. The exclusion does not decide the pair, because condition 3 already fails.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation, shown by P-79 to produce the headline gap: adding T1 grey-matter volumes to fMRI raises NC vs LMCI accuracy from 87.59% to 97.44%. Because a paper shows this, the pair fails condition 3.
candidate_explanations.quote: the multimodal model achieved an ACC of 97.44%, an AUC of 99.75%, and an F1-score of 97.22%, representing improvements of approximately 9.9%, 5.7%, and 11.4%, respectively, compared to the fMRI-only setting

candidate_explanations.difference: Longitudinal input in P-71: a second (year-1) scan raises its accuracy from 87.14% to 91.42% on ADNI-2&3.
candidate_explanations.quote: All the detection tasks have three different scenarios: baseline, year1, and their fusion.

reason: Once the record's misreading ('+8.5%' is an improvement margin, not an accuracy) is corrected, the pair compares P-71's 91.42% with P-79's 97.44% for LMCI vs NC. That gap is beyond uncertainty, but both papers report the shared single-time-point rs-fMRI condition, and there they agree (87.30%/87.14% against 87.59%). P-79's own ablation assigns the rest of the gap to its added T1 input. The pair fails condition 3. P-79's headline figure would also fall under the Section 3.5 exclusion.

quotes.quote: achieving an average improvement of 8.5% in accuracy over baseline models.
The dataset includes 161 normal controls (NC), 147 early mild cognitive impairment (EMCI) subjects, and 128 late mild cognitive impairment (LMCI) subjects.
We adopted stratified five-fold cross-validation to evaluate model performance.

we selected data from the Southwest University site (SITE-20) of the publicly available multi-center REST-META-MDD dataset (Yan et al., 2019), comprising 282 patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and 251 Healthy Controls (HC).
Due to the small dataset, the leave one out cross validation (LOOCV) is used in the experiments.
